title: Perception, processing, and modulation of painful and non-painful somatosensory stimuli
summary: There is a close connection between our perception of pain and our perception of our own body. For example, looking at a part of one’s own body can have a pain-relieving effect, while chronic pain is often associated with an altered perception of one’s own body. However, the underlying mechanisms are not yet sufficiently understood. It is assumed that the body’s own ability to inhibit or amplify pain—known as endogenous pain modulation—plays a crucial role. Therefore, in this study, the endogenous pain modulation of healthy participants will be measured while their body perception is manipulated in various ways. The aim of the study is to investigate how psychological factors—such as altered body perception—can influence the experience of pain.

interventions.name: Participants will either look at their own left hand (experimental condition) or at one of several objects (control conditions).
